    87→/**
    88→ * @brief Create a constant reactive variable wrapping the given value.
    89→ *
    90→ * This is similar to var(), but the wrapped value is const.
    91→ * The reactive node is registered to the ObserverGraph.
    92→ *
    93→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
    94→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
    95→ * @tparam SrcType The type of the source value.
    96→ * @param t The value to wrap as a const reactive variable.
    97→ * @return React<VarExpr, const std::remove_cvref_t<SrcType>, IV, TR> Reactive constant wrapper.
    98→ */
    99→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, NonReact SrcType>
   100→auto constVar(SrcType &&t) {
   101→    auto ptr = std::make_shared<ReactImpl<VarExpr, const std::remove_cvref_t<SrcType>, IV, TR>>(std::forward<SrcType>(t));
   102→    ObserverGraph::getInstance().addNode(ptr);
   103→    return React{ptr};
   104→}

   106→/**
   107→ * @brief Create a reactive variable wrapping the given value.
   108→ *
   109→ * If the source type supports the Field concept, binds the field in the FieldGraph.
   110→ * Registers the reactive node to the ObserverGraph.
   111→ *
   112→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
   113→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
   114→ * @tparam SrcType The type of the source value.
   115→ * @param t The value to wrap reactively.
   116→ * @return React<VarExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<SrcType>, IV, TR> Reactive variable wrapper.
   117→ */
   118→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, NonReact SrcType>
   119→auto var(SrcType &&t) {
   120→    REACTION_REGISTER_THREAD();
   121→    auto ptr = std::make_shared<ReactImpl<VarExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<SrcType>, IV, TR>>(std::forward<SrcType>(t));
   122→    ObserverGraph::getInstance().addNode(ptr);
   123→    if constexpr (HasField<SrcType>) {
   124→        FieldGraph::getInstance().bindField(t.getId(), ptr->shared_from_this());
   125→    }
   126→    return React{ptr};
   127→}
   128→
   129→/**
   130→ * @brief Create a reactive expression wrapping the given operator expression.
   131→ *
   132→ * Registers the node to ObserverGraph, then sets (evaluates) the expression immediately.
   133→ * Supports both binary and unary operator expressions.
   134→ *
   135→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
   136→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
   137→ * @tparam OpExpr The operator expression type (binary or unary).
   138→ * @param opExpr The operator expression to wrap.
   139→ * @return React<CalcExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<OpExpr>, IV, TR> Reactive calculation wrapper.
   140→ */
   141→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, IsOpExpr OpExpr>
   142→auto expr(OpExpr &&opExpr) {
   143→    REACTION_REGISTER_THREAD();
   144→    auto ptr = std::make_shared<ReactImpl<CalcExpr, std::remove_cvref_t<OpExpr>, IV, TR>>(std::forward<OpExpr>(opExpr));
   145→    ObserverGraph::getInstance().addNode(ptr);
   146→    ptr->set();
   147→    return React{ptr};
   148→}
   149→
   150→/**
   151→ * @brief Create a reactive calculation based on a callable and its arguments.
   152→ *
   153→ * Registers the node to ObserverGraph and immediately sets (evaluates) the calculation.
   154→ *
   155→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
   156→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
   157→ * @tparam Fun Callable type.
   158→ * @tparam Args Argument types for the callable.
   159→ * @param fun The callable to invoke reactively.
   160→ * @param args Arguments to forward to the callable.
   161→ * @return React<CalcExpr, ReturnType<Fun, Args...>, IV, TR> Reactive calculation wrapper.
   162→ */
   163→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, typename Fun, typename... Args>
   164→auto calc(Fun &&fun, Args &&...args) {
   165→    REACTION_REGISTER_THREAD();
   166→    auto ptr = std::make_shared<ReactImpl<CalcExpr, ReturnType<Fun, Args...>, IV, TR>>();
   167→    ObserverGraph::getInstance().addNode(ptr);
   168→    ptr->set(std::forward<Fun>(fun), std::forward<Args>(args)...);
   169→    return React{ptr};
   170→}
   171→
   172→/**
   173→ * @brief Alias for calc(), used to create a reactive action.
   174→ *
   175→ * @tparam TR Trigger mode, default is ChangeTrig.
   176→ * @tparam IV Invalidation strategy, default is KeepHandle.
   177→ * @tparam Fun Callable type.
   178→ * @tparam Args Argument types.
   179→ * @param fun The callable to invoke reactively.
   180→ * @param args Arguments to forward to the callable.
   181→ * @return The reactive action wrapper.
   182→ */
   183→template <IsTrigger TR = ChangeTrig, IsInvalidation IV = KeepHandle, typename Fun, typename... Args>
   184→auto action(Fun &&fun, Args &&...args) {
   185→    return calc<TR, IV>(std::forward<Fun>(fun), std::forward<Args>(args)...);
   186→}
   187→
   188→/**
   189→ * @brief Factory function to create a reactive wrapper from a value or expression.
   190→ *
   191→ * If the input is a binary operator expression, creates an expr().
   192→ * If the input is an invocable callable, creates a calc().
   193→ * Otherwise, creates a var().
   194→ *
   195→ * @tparam T The type of input.
   196→ * @param t The input value, expression, or callable.
   197→ * @return Corresponding reactive wrapper.
   198→ */
   199→template <NonReact T>
   200→auto create(T &&t) {
   201→    if constexpr (IsBinaryOpExpr<std::remove_cvref_t<T>>) {
   202→        return expr(std::forward<T>(t));
   203→    } else if constexpr (InvocableType<T>) {
   204→        return calc(std::forward<T>(t));
   205→    } else {
   206→        return var(std::forward<T>(t));
   207→    }
   208→}
   209→
   210→/**
   211→ * @brief Factory function to create a reactive calculation from a callable and arguments.
   212→ *
   213→ * This function wraps a callable and its arguments into a reactive calculation,
   214→ * which automatically updates when any of its dependencies change.
   215→ *
   216→ * @tparam Fun Callable type.
   217→ * @tparam Args Argument types to be forwarded to the callable.
   218→ * @param fun The callable to invoke reactively.
   219→ * @param args Arguments to forward to the callable.
   220→ * @return A reactive calculation wrapper.
   221→ */
   222→template <typename Fun, typename... Args>
   223→auto create(Fun &&fun, Args &&...args) {
   224→    return calc(std::forward<Fun>(fun), std::forward<Args>(args)...);
   225→}
   226→
   227→/**
   228→ * @brief Begins a batch of reactive updates.
   229→ *
   230→ * This function creates a batch context, deferring propagation of reactive updates
   231→ * until the batch is executed. Useful for grouping multiple changes together efficiently.
   232→ *
   233→ * @tparam Fun Callable type to execute within the batch.
   234→ * @param fun A function containing batched operations.
   235→ * @return A Batch object encapsulating the operation.
   236→ */
   237→template <InvocableType Fun>
   238→auto batch(Fun &&fun) {
   239→    return Batch{std::forward<Fun>(fun)};
   240→}
   241→
   242→/**
   243→ * @brief Immediately executes a batch of reactive updates.
   244→ *
   245→ * This function creates a batch context and executes it immediately.
   246→ * Any reactive updates are postponed until the end of the batch execution.
   247→ *
   248→ * @tparam Fun Callable type to execute within the batch.
   249→ * @param fun A function containing batched operations to be executed.
   250→ */
   251→template <InvocableType Fun>
   252→void batchExecute(Fun &&fun) {
   253→    Batch batch{std::forward<Fun>(fun)};
   254→    batch.execute();
   255→}
   256→
   257→} // namespace reaction
   258→

    12→#include "reaction/expression/expression_types.h"
    13→#include "reaction/expression/operators.h"
    14→
    15→namespace reaction {
    16→
    17→/**
    18→ * @brief Creates a binary expression from two operands and an operator.
    19→ *
    20→ * Optimized factory function with perfect forwarding and compile-time optimization.
    21→ *
    22→ * @tparam Op The operator type
    23→ * @tparam L Left operand type
    24→ * @tparam R Right operand type
    25→ * @param l Left operand
    26→ * @param r Right operand
    27→ * @return Binary expression with optimized type deduction
    28→ */
    29→template <typename Op, typename L, typename R>
    30→[[nodiscard]] constexpr auto make_binary_expr(L &&l, R &&r) noexcept(
    31→    std::is_nothrow_constructible_v<BinaryOpExpr<Op, ExprTraits<std::remove_cvref_t<L>>, ExprTraits<std::remove_cvref_t<R>>>, L, R>) {
    32→    using LeftType = ExprTraits<std::remove_cvref_t<L>>;
    33→    using RightType = ExprTraits<std::remove_cvref_t<R>>;
    34→    return BinaryOpExpr<Op, LeftType, RightType>(std::forward<L>(l), std::forward<R>(r));
    35→}
    36→
    37→/**
    38→ * @brief Creates a unary expression from one operand and an operator.
    39→ *
    40→ * Optimized factory function with perfect forwarding and compile-time optimization.
    41→ *
    42→ * @tparam Op The operator type
    43→ * @tparam T Operand type
    44→ * @param operand The operand
    45→ * @return Unary expression with optimized type deduction
    46→ */
    47→template <typename Op, typename T>
    48→[[nodiscard]] constexpr auto make_unary_expr(T &&operand) noexcept(
    49→    std::is_nothrow_constructible_v<UnaryOpExpr<Op, ExprTraits<std::remove_cvref_t<T>>>, T>) {
    50→    using OperandType = ExprTraits<std::remove_cvref_t<T>>;
    51→    return UnaryOpExpr<Op, OperandType>(std::forward<T>(operand));
    52→}
    53→
    54→// === Generic Binary Operator Overload Template ===
    55→
    56→/**
    57→ * @brief Generic template for binary operator overloads.
    58→ *
    59→ * Reduces code duplication by providing a unified implementation for all binary operators.
    60→ *
    61→ * @tparam Op The operator type (AddOp, MulOp, etc.)
    62→ * @tparam L Left operand type
    63→ * @tparam R Right operand type
    64→ */
    65→template <typename Op, typename L, typename R>
    66→    requires HasReactOp<L, R>
    67→constexpr auto make_binary_op(L &&l, R &&r) {
    68→    return make_binary_expr<Op>(std::forward<L>(l), std::forward<R>(r));
    69→}
    70→
    71→// === Operator Overload Generation Macros ===
    72→
    73→/**
    74→ * @brief Macro to generate binary operator overloads.
    75→ *
    76→ * @param op_symbol The C++ operator symbol
    77→ * @param OpType The corresponding operator functor type
    78→ */
    79→#define REACTION_DEFINE_BINARY_OPERATOR(op_symbol, OpType)                     \
    80→    template <typename L, typename R>                                          \
    81→        requires HasReactOp<L, R>                                              \
    82→    constexpr auto operator op_symbol(L &&l, R &&r) {                          \
    83→        return make_binary_op<OpType>(std::forward<L>(l), std::forward<R>(r)); \
    84→    }
    85→
    86→/**
    87→ * @brief Macro to generate unary operator overloads.
    88→ *
    89→ * @param op_symbol The C++ operator symbol
    90→ * @param OpType The corresponding operator functor type
    91→ */
    92→#define REACTION_DEFINE_UNARY_OPERATOR(op_symbol, OpType)                                                                           \
    93→    template <typename T>                                                                                                           \
    94→        requires IsReact<std::remove_cvref_t<T>> || IsBinaryOpExpr<std::remove_cvref_t<T>> || IsUnaryOpExpr<std::remove_cvref_t<T>> \
    95→    constexpr auto operator op_symbol(T &&operand) {                                                                                \
    96→        return make_unary_op<OpType>(std::forward<T>(operand));                                                                     \
    97→    }
    98→
    99→// === Arithmetic Operators ===
   100→
   101→REACTION_DEFINE_BINARY_OPERATOR(+, AddOp);
   102→REACTION_DEFINE_BINARY_OPERATOR(*, MulOp);
   103→REACTION_DEFINE_BINARY_OPERATOR(-, SubOp);
   104→REACTION_DEFINE_BINARY_OPERATOR(/, DivOp);
   105→
   106→// === Comparison Operators ===
   107→
   108→REACTION_DEFINE_BINARY_OPERATOR(==, EqOp);
   109→REACTION_DEFINE_BINARY_OPERATOR(!=, NeOp);
   110→REACTION_DEFINE_BINARY_OPERATOR(<, LtOp);
   111→REACTION_DEFINE_BINARY_OPERATOR(>, GtOp);
   112→REACTION_DEFINE_BINARY_OPERATOR(<=, LeOp);
   113→REACTION_DEFINE_BINARY_OPERATOR(>=, GeOp);
   114→
   115→// === Logical Operators ===
   116→
   117→REACTION_DEFINE_BINARY_OPERATOR(&&, AndOp);
   118→REACTION_DEFINE_BINARY_OPERATOR(||, OrOp);
   119→
   120→// === Generic Unary Operator Helper ===
   121→
   122→/**
   123→ * @brief Generic template for unary operator overloads.
   124→ *
   125→ * @tparam Op The operator type (NegOp, NotOp, etc.)
   126→ * @tparam T Operand type
   127→ */
   128→template <typename Op, typename T>
   129→    requires IsReact<std::remove_cvref_t<T>> || IsBinaryOpExpr<std::remove_cvref_t<T>> || IsUnaryOpExpr<std::remove_cvref_t<T>>
   130→constexpr auto make_unary_op(T &&operand) {
   131→    return make_unary_expr<Op>(std::forward<T>(operand));
   132→}
   133→
   134→// === Unary Operators ===
   135→
   136→REACTION_DEFINE_UNARY_OPERATOR(-, NegOp);
   137→REACTION_DEFINE_UNARY_OPERATOR(!, NotOp);
   138→REACTION_DEFINE_UNARY_OPERATOR(~, BitNotOp);
   139→
   140→// Cleanup macros to avoid namespace pollution
   141→#undef REACTION_DEFINE_BINARY_OPERATOR
   142→#undef REACTION_DEFINE_UNARY_OPERATOR
   143→
   144→} // namespace reaction

    10→#include <type_traits>
    11→#include <utility>
    12→
    13→namespace reaction {
    14→
    15→// === Base Templates for Operator Categories ===
    16→
    17→/**
    18→ * @brief Base template for binary operators with automatic forwarding.
    19→ *
    20→ * @tparam Derived The derived operator type (CRTP)
    21→ */
    22→template <typename Derived>
    23→struct BinaryOperatorBase {
    24→    template <typename L, typename R>
    25→    constexpr auto operator()(L &&l, R &&r) const noexcept(noexcept(static_cast<const Derived *>(this)->apply(std::forward<L>(l), std::forward<R>(r)))) {
    26→        return static_cast<const Derived *>(this)->apply(std::forward<L>(l), std::forward<R>(r));
    27→    }
    28→};
    29→
    30→/**
    31→ * @brief Base template for unary operators with automatic forwarding.
    32→ *
    33→ * @tparam Derived The derived operator type (CRTP)
    34→ */
    35→template <typename Derived>
    36→struct UnaryOperatorBase {
    37→    template <typename T>
    38→    constexpr auto operator()(T &&operand) const noexcept(noexcept(static_cast<const Derived *>(this)->apply(std::forward<T>(operand)))) {
    39→        return static_cast<const Derived *>(this)->apply(std::forward<T>(operand));
    40→    }
    41→};
    42→
    43→// === Operator Generation Macro ===
    44→
    45→/**
    46→ * @brief Macro to generate simple binary operators with automatic noexcept deduction.
    47→ *
    48→ * @param OpName The operator class name
    49→ * @param symbol The C++ operator symbol
    50→ * @param description Human-readable description
    51→ */
    52→#define REACTION_DEFINE_BINARY_OP(OpName, symbol, description)                    \
    53→    /** @brief description */                                                     \
    54→    struct OpName : BinaryOperatorBase<OpName> {                                  \
    55→        template <typename L, typename R>                                         \
    56→        constexpr auto apply(L &&l, R &&r) const noexcept(noexcept(l symbol r)) { \
    57→            return l symbol r;                                                    \
    58→        }                                                                         \
    59→    }
    60→
    61→// === Arithmetic Operators ===
    62→

    14→
    15→// === Base Templates for Operator Categories ===
    16→
    17→/**
    18→ * @brief Base template for binary operators with automatic forwarding.
    19→ *
    20→ * @tparam Derived The derived operator type (CRTP)
    21→ */
    22→template <typename Derived>
    23→struct BinaryOperatorBase {
    24→    template <typename L, typename R>
    25→    constexpr auto operator()(L &&l, R &&r) const noexcept(noexcept(static_cast<const Derived *>(this)->apply(std::forward<L>(l), std::forward<R>(r)))) {
    26→        return static_cast<const Derived *>(this)->apply(std::forward<L>(l), std::forward<R>(r));
    27→    }
    28→};
    29→
    30→/**
    31→ * @brief Base template for unary operators with automatic forwarding.
    32→ *
    33→ * @tparam Derived The derived operator type (CRTP)
    34→ */
    35→template <typename Derived>
    36→struct UnaryOperatorBase {
    37→    template <typename T>
    38→    constexpr auto operator()(T &&operand) const noexcept(noexcept(static_cast<const Derived *>(this)->apply(std::forward<T>(operand)))) {
    39→        return static_cast<const Derived *>(this)->apply(std::forward<T>(operand));
    40→    }
    41→};
    42→
    43→// === Operator Generation Macro ===
    44→
    45→/**
    46→ * @brief Macro to generate simple binary operators with automatic noexcept deduction.
    47→ *
    48→ * @param OpName The operator class name
    49→ * @param symbol The C++ operator symbol
    50→ * @param description Human-readable description
    51→ */
    52→#define REACTION_DEFINE_BINARY_OP(OpName, symbol, description)                    \
    53→    /** @brief description */                                                     \
    54→    struct OpName : BinaryOperatorBase<OpName> {                                  \
    55→        template <typename L, typename R>                                         \
    56→        constexpr auto apply(L &&l, R &&r) const noexcept(noexcept(l symbol r)) { \
    57→            return l symbol r;                                                    \
    58→        }                                                                         \
    59→    }
    60→
    61→// === Arithmetic Operators ===
    62→
    63→REACTION_DEFINE_BINARY_OP(AddOp, +, Addition operator functor for reactive expressions);
    64→REACTION_DEFINE_BINARY_OP(MulOp, *, Multiplication operator functor for reactive expressions);
    65→REACTION_DEFINE_BINARY_OP(SubOp, -, Subtraction operator functor for reactive expressions);
    66→
    67→/**
    68→ * @brief Division operator functor for reactive expressions.
    69→ *
    70→ * Performs division operation between two operands with floating-point precision.
    71→ * For integer operands, promotes to double to ensure floating-point division.
    72→ * Note: Division by zero behavior depends on the operand types.
    73→ */
    74→struct DivOp : BinaryOperatorBase<DivOp> {
    75→    template <typename L, typename R>
    76→    constexpr auto apply(L &&l, R &&r) const {
    77→        using L_t = std::remove_cvref_t<L>;
    78→        using R_t = std::remove_cvref_t<R>;
    79→
    80→        // If both operands are integral types, promote to double for floating-point division
    81→        if constexpr (std::is_integral_v<L_t> && std::is_integral_v<R_t>) {
    82→            return static_cast<double>(l) / static_cast<double>(r);
    83→        } else {
    84→            return l / r;
    85→        }
    86→    }
    87→};
    88→
    89→// === Comparison Operators ===
    90→
    91→REACTION_DEFINE_BINARY_OP(EqOp, ==, Equality comparison operator functor for reactive expressions);
    92→REACTION_DEFINE_BINARY_OP(NeOp, !=, Inequality comparison operator functor for reactive expressions);
    93→REACTION_DEFINE_BINARY_OP(LtOp, <, Less than comparison operator functor for reactive expressions);
    94→REACTION_DEFINE_BINARY_OP(GtOp, >, Greater than comparison operator functor for reactive expressions);
    95→REACTION_DEFINE_BINARY_OP(LeOp, <=, Less than or equal comparison operator functor for reactive expressions);
    96→REACTION_DEFINE_BINARY_OP(GeOp, >=, Greater than or equal comparison operator functor for reactive expressions);
    97→
    98→// === Logical Operators ===
    99→
   100→REACTION_DEFINE_BINARY_OP(AndOp, &&, Logical AND operator functor for reactive expressions);
   101→REACTION_DEFINE_BINARY_OP(OrOp, ||, Logical OR operator functor for reactive expressions);
   102→
   103→// === Unary Operator Generation Macro ===
   104→
   105→/**
   106→ * @brief Macro to generate simple unary operators with automatic noexcept deduction.
   107→ *
   108→ * @param OpName The operator class name
   109→ * @param symbol The C++ operator symbol
   110→ * @param description Human-readable description
   111→ */
   112→#define REACTION_DEFINE_UNARY_OP(OpName, symbol, description)                        \
   113→    /** @brief description */                                                        \
   114→    struct OpName : UnaryOperatorBase<OpName> {                                      \
   115→        template <typename T>                                                        \
   116→        constexpr auto apply(T &&operand) const noexcept(noexcept(symbol operand)) { \
   117→            return symbol operand;                                                   \
   118→        }                                                                            \
   119→    }
   120→
   121→// === Unary Operators ===
   122→
   123→REACTION_DEFINE_UNARY_OP(NegOp, -, Unary negation operator functor for reactive expressions);
   124→REACTION_DEFINE_UNARY_OP(NotOp, !, Logical NOT operator functor for reactive expressions);
   125→REACTION_DEFINE_UNARY_OP(BitNotOp, ~, Bitwise NOT operator functor for reactive expressions);
   126→
   127→// Cleanup macros to avoid pollution
   128→#undef REACTION_DEFINE_BINARY_OP
   129→#undef REACTION_DEFINE_UNARY_OP
